title: The Life of a Ballot MD
text: Bal󰈗󰈡󰉄* The life of a *Maryland Edition How a Ballot becomes a Vote* *in Maryland Action taken by: As an election approaches... Voter Election Official Ballots are prepared Voters choose how they will vote Military and Overseas Citizens UOCAVA Mail-In Voting Early Voting Election Day Voters apply for Voters make sure their a mail-in ballot registration re�lects their UOCAVA status Mail -in ballots are issued in the manner Voters cast a ballot at chosen by the voter a polling place UOCAVA ballots Voters cast a ballot at are issued an early voting center Voters complete and return mail-in ballots Voters complete and return their ballot If needed, voters cure If needed, voters their provisional ballot cure their ballot Election Day ballots Mail-in ballots are processed are processed If needed, voters cure If needed, voters their provisional ballot cure their ballot Early Voting ballots UOCAVA ballots are processed are processed Votes are Counted! 2 Mail in Voting Voters apply for a mail in ballot ● Any registered Maryland voter may request a mail-in ballot with no reason required. There are three ways to apply: ○ A voter may go to their local board of elections and receive a mail-in ballot in person ○ Voters that have a Maryland driver’s license or MVA-issued ID card may request a ballot online ○ A voter can complete and sign a mail-in ballot application that can be returned via mail, fax, email, or in person with an attached image of their signed request to their local board ● These requests may take about a week to process. Voters may also sign up for the permanent mail-in ballot list. In future elections they are eligible to vote in, they will automatically receive a mail-in ballot without needing to submit a new request each time.

title: The Life of a Ballot MD
text: Voters may also sign up for the permanent mail-in ballot list. In future elections they are eligible to vote in, they will automatically receive a mail-in ballot without needing to submit a new request each time. Mail in ballots are issued in the manner chosen by the voter ● Once a voter’s application for a ballot is processed, the ballot is issued by the method the voter chose to receive it (web delivery, fax or by mail). ● Voters who received the ballot by mail or fax will fill the oval to the left of their choice on the ballot with black pen. Those who downloaded their ballots from SBE’s website can print the blank ballot and mark it by hand. ● It is important for voters to make sure not to sign their names or make any other identifying marks on the ballot. Voters complete and return mail-in ballots ● Voters who received a by mail ballot are provided with a prepaid postage return envelope for their voted ballot. ● Voters who received a fax or web delivered ballot should use the envelope template provided in their ballot materials for their return envelope. ● We recommend that voters return their ballots as soon as they have voted. There are three ways to return a mail in ballot: 1. Mail a ballot which must be postmarked on or before election day. 2. Use a ballot dropbox in which a ballot must be in a dropbox by 8pm on Election Day 3 3. Hand deliver a ballot to a local board of elections or voting location in which you must deliver your ballot by 8pm on Election Day. ● Voters cannot email or fax their voted mail-in ballot.

title: The Life of a Ballot MD
text: Use a ballot dropbox in which a ballot must be in a dropbox by 8pm on Election Day 3 3. Hand deliver a ballot to a local board of elections or voting location in which you must deliver your ballot by 8pm on Election Day. ● Voters cannot email or fax their voted mail-in ballot. If needed, voters cure their ballot ● This occurs when a ballot is missing a signature on the return envelope oath. Before the votes are counted, the board checks envelopes for the voter’s signature, and if no signature is found the board will reach out to the voter to request a signed oath. ● Voters may then submit a signed oath back to the board of elections by 10 a.m. on the last day of canvass. If the voter does not provide a signed oath by the deadline, their ballot will not be counted. ● In Maryland, there is a Text2Cure program that allows voters to receive a text message prompting them to cure their ballot. Voters then click a link, sign electronically and submit their oath via their phone. Mail-in ballots are processed ● Processing mail-in ballots is known as “canvassing.” Bipartisan members of local boards of elections meet as the board of canvassers and members of the public may attend. ● Canvassing begins 8 days before early voting starts. There are additional canvassing days after Election Day, but Canvass will not be held on Election Day. ● Teams of two people from different political parties review ballots, verifying that they were returned on time and that the voter signed the oath. If both conditions are met, the envelope is opened to ensure it can be read by the scanner.

title: The Life of a Ballot MD
text: There are additional canvassing days after Election Day, but Canvass will not be held on Election Day. ● Teams of two people from different political parties review ballots, verifying that they were returned on time and that the voter signed the oath. If both conditions are met, the envelope is opened to ensure it can be read by the scanner. Should a ballot not be clear, the ballot is given to the local board where they will follow the regulations to define the validity of a vote. ● If a ballot cannot be scanned, a team creates an identical duplicate ballot that the scanner can read, with team members verifying each other’s work. ● Examples of why ballots must be rejected include if they are not timely received, the voter failed to sign the oath or submit a signed oath on time, or a voter returned multiple ballots in the same envelope. 4 Early Voting Voters cast a ballot at an early voting center ● Any person that is registered or eligible to register can vote during early voting. ● For both primary and general elections, voters may cast their ballot at any early voting center in the county that they live in. ● The process for early voting is the same as voting on election day. When a voter gets to the early voting center, they will check in to vote and cast their ballot. If needed, voters cast a provisional ballot ● A provisional ballot is issued when there is a question about a voter’s eligibility at the time they try to vote.

title: The Life of a Ballot MD
text: When a voter gets to the early voting center, they will check in to vote and cast their ballot. If needed, voters cast a provisional ballot ● A provisional ballot is issued when there is a question about a voter’s eligibility at the time they try to vote. Some common reasons for this include not being registered to vote, moving and not updating an address, claiming a different party affiliation and not providing an ID when asked. ● Provisional ballots are not counted immediately. Election officials start counting these ballots on the second Wednesday after each election. They will count as long as a voter is registered, eligible to vote by provisional ballot, and meet any other applicable requirements. Early Voting ballots are processed ● Regular ballots that are cast during early voting are scanned and counted as part of the standard vote-counting process. ● Early Voting results will be included in the first batch of election results on Election Night. ● Provisional ballots from early voting are counted separately. 5 Election Day Voters cast a ballot at a polling place ● On Election Day, voters must go to their assigned polling place between 7 a.m. and 8 p.m. If a voter is in line before 8, they may stay in line until they cast their vote. ● Those who are voting may bring children under 18 and any printed material, including a marked specimen ballot, to help them vote. ● Voters may not use cell phones, pagers, cameras, or computer equipment except to use as a translation device, proof of residency or ID, or review election information, and to record a digital image of their ballot prior to casting for personal use.

title: The Life of a Ballot MD
text: If needed, voters cast a provisional ballot ● On Election Day, a voter may need to cast a provisional ballot if their eligibility cannot be confirmed at the polling place. This may be due to a variety of reasons such as their name not appearing on voter rolls, moving and not updating registration, claiming a different party affiliation or if they had a mail-in ballot on record. ● Provisional ballots from Election Day are returned to the local board of elections with election judge materials on Election Night. Election Day ballots are processed ● After polls close on Election Day, election workers secure all ballots and equipment at the polling place. ● Regular ballots that were cast on Election Day are counted by the scanner at the polling place as they are submitted throughout the day. ● Ballots and all materials are returned to the local board of elections after the polls close so unofficial election results can be generated for the public. 6 UOCAVA Voters make sure their registration reflects their UOCAVA status ■ A Uniformed Services voter is a U.S. citizen who is a member of (or the spouse or dependent of a member of) the: ○ Uniformed Services (Army, Navy, Air Force, Marines, and Coast Guard); ○ Merchant marine; ○ Commissioned corps of the Public Health Service; and ○ National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration ■ An overseas voter is a citizen who resides outside of the United States and its territories and but for residence, would be otherwise qualified to vote in Maryland. ● UOCAVA voters should verify their voter registration is current and reflects their UOCAVA status before each election.

title: The Life of a Ballot MD
text: Voters can check their registration status through the Maryland Voter Lookup tool. ● Maryland residents who are serving in the Uniformed Services or residing outside of the United States, but still wish to register and vote in Maryland may do so. UOCAVA ballots are issued ● Ballots are mailed, faxed, or can be downloaded from the State’s website. ● We recommend submitting UOCAVA ballot requests as early as possible. ● Federal law requires that Maryland send ballots to UOCAVA voters at least 45 days prior to a federal election. Voters complete and return their ballots ● The way a UOCAVA voter requests their mail-in ballot determines how they return them. If a voter downloaded their ballot from the State’s website, they can print the blank ballot and mark it by hand. If they received the ballot by mail or fax, they will write with black pen, filling in the oval to the left of their choice. ● To return a ballot, UOCAVA voters must mail or hand deliver their ballot to their local board of elections, a ballot drop off box, an early voting center, or an election day polling place in the county where they live.

title: The Life of a Ballot MD
text: The process is similar to the regular mail-in voting process, with no submissions of voted ballots online or returned by email or fax. ● If a voter is mailing their ballot via a foreign mail system, they must make sure that the return envelope has the proper postage included. 7 UOCAVA ballots are processed ● UOCAVA ballots go through the same process as other mail-in ballots, where local election officials verify that the ballot was received in time and that the voter signed their oath, then opens and scans the ballot. ● UOCAVA ballots that arrive after Election Day may still be counted as long as they are postmarked by Election Day and received within the timeframe set. ● Voters can visit the voter look-up website to verify the status of their UOCAVA ballot.

title: SBE Primary Early Voting Ends 2026 06 18
text:
Jared DeMarinis Michael Summers, Chairman
State Administrator
Jim Shalleck, Vice Chair
Diane Butler
Katherine Berry
Victoria Jackson-Stanley
Deputy Administrator
Eric Bryant
In-Person Early Voting in Maryland’s
Primary Election Ends Tomorrow
ANNAPOLIS (June 17, 2026) — The Maryland State Board of Elections (SBE) reminds voters that
in-person early voting in the Gubernatorial Primary Election ends tomorrow, Thursday June 18.
“With the end of early voting approaching, I remind any Marylander who wants to vote early to plan
ahead,” said Jared DeMarinis, Administrator of State Elections. “Find your early voting center by
visiting our website or by downloading our free Go Vote Maryland! app.”
Early voting will run from 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. Thursday. Voters in line by 8 p.m. can cast a ballot. A list
of early voting centers is available online at vote.md.gov/vote2026.
SBE also reminds Marylanders who are not registered to vote that they can register when casting a
ballot. Make sure to bring a document that proves where you live when you attempt to vote at your
local polling place or early voting center.
Early voting is one of three options to cast your ballot in this election. The other two are mail-in
voting and in-person voting on Primary Election Day, Tuesday, June 23. Learn more about these
options and the primary election at vote.md.gov/vote2026 or download the free Go Vote Maryland!
app from the Google Play store or the Apple store.

title: SBE Primary Early Voting Starts June 2026
text:
Jared DeMarinis Michael Summers, Chairman
State Administrator
Jim Shalleck, Vice Chair
Diane Butler
Katherine Berry
Victoria Jackson-Stanley
Deputy Administrator
Eric Bryant
In-Person Early Voting in Maryland’s
Primary Election Starts Tomorrow
ANNAPOLIS (June 10, 2026) — The Maryland State Board of Elections (SBE) reminds voters that
in-person early voting in the Gubernatorial Primary Election begins tomorrow, Thursday June 11.
“Early voting is a secure and convenient option for casting your vote in the primary election,” said
Jared DeMarinis, State Administrator of Elections. “We typically experience strong turnout for early
voting, so I urge every Marylander considering this option to plan ahead.”
Early voting runs from Thursday, June 11 to Thursday, June 18 from 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. daily. Voters
who are in line by 8 p.m. can cast a ballot. A complete list of early voting centers is available online
at vote.md.gov/vote2026.
There is still time to register to vote in the primary election. Marylanders can register when they cast
their vote during early voting or on Primary Election Day (Tuesday, June 23.) Make sure to bring a
document that proves where you live when you attempt to vote at your local polling place or early
voting center.
Early voting is one of three options to cast your ballot in this election. The other two are mail-in
voting and in-person voting on Primary Election Day, Tuesday, June 23. For additional information
about these options and the primary election, visit vote.md.gov/vote2026 or download the free Go
Vote Maryland! app from the Google Play store or the Apple store.

text:
Jared DeMarinis Michael Summers, Chairman
State Administrator

Diane Butler
Katherine Berry

Eric Bryant
Deadline to Request a Mail-in Ballot is Approaching
ANNAPOLIS (June 2, 2026) — The Maryland State Board of Elections reminds voters that the
deadline to request a mail-in ballot for the 2026 Gubernatorial Primary Election is approaching.
To receive your mail-in ballot via mail or fax, your request must be received (not just mailed) or
submitted online by June 16, 2026. If you want to receive your mail-in ballot via email, submit your
request online by Friday, June 19, 2026. Visit SBE’s mail-in ballot webpage to request a ballot.
Mail-in ballots returned by mail must be postmarked by or before 8 p.m. on Primary Election Day,
Tuesday, June 23. If returned by hand, ballots must be submitted at an early voting center during
early voting, or dropped at a ballot drop box or local board of elections by 8 p.m. on June 23. A list of
locations can be found at vote.md.gov/vote2026.
“As the Primary Election approaches, I encourage every registered voter to make sure they have a
plan to vote,” said State Administrator of Elections Jared DeMarinis, . “Mail-in ballots are a secure,
legal, and transparent option for casting your vote. Be sure to request your ballot before the
deadline.”
Registered voters have two other options for casting their vote: vote early in-person or vote on
Primary Election Day.
1. Vote Early In-Person: Avoid the Election Day rush by voting early.
Dates: Thursday, June 11 through Thursday, June 18
Hours: 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. daily.
If you are in line by 8 p.m. you will be permitted to cast a ballot. A complete list of early voting
centers is available at vote.md.gov/vote2026
2. Election Day In-Person: Vote in person at your local polling place on Primary Election Day,
Tuesday, June 23.
Hours: Polls are open from 7 a.m. to 8 p.m.
Voters must cast their vote at their assigned polling place. Locate your polling place on the SBE
website.
Voters who requested a mail-in ballot before May 14 are reminded to vote the replacement ballot
sent at the end of May. Mark and return the replacement ballot to ensure the correct party ballot is
counted. To track the status of your ballot visit vote.md.gov/search. Additional information about
Maryland’s Primary Election, including deadlines to return your voted ballot, can be found at

title: SBE Mail In Ballot Canvass Primary 2026
text:
Jared DeMarinis Michael Summers, Chairman
State Administrator
Jim Shalleck, Vice Chair
Diane Butler
Katherine Berry
Victoria Jackson-Stanley
Deputy Administrator
Eric Bryant
Canvassing of Mail-In Ballots for
Primary Election to Begin June 1
Voters Are Reminded to Vote Replacement Mail-In Ballots Mailed the Week of May 24
ANNAPOLIS (May 29, 2026) — Monday, June 1 marks the first day that mail-in ballots will be
canvassed for the 2026 Gubernatorial Primary Election. Local boards of elections can begin the
process of opening, reviewing, and counting ballots that have been returned by Monday, June 1.
According to Maryland law, local boards of elections may meet eight business days prior to the start
of Early Voting – June 11 – to begin canvassing mail-in ballots that have been returned. Members of
the public may observe the canvass.
Additional canvassing days may take place after this time, but are not to be held on Primary Election
Day, June 23. All mail-in ballots postmarked on or before June 23 will be canvassed. Results of the
canvass are not made public until after polls close at 8 p.m. on Election Day.
Local boards post on their websites the dates, times and locations of their canvasses. For more
information about a local board’s canvassing timeline, please contact the local board. To learn more
about the vote canvassing process in Maryland, visit SBE’s canvassing webpage.
“Mail-in voting is a legal, secure, and transparent method to cast your vote in this election,” said State
Administrator Jared DeMarinis. “June 1 is the first day in a transparent and deliberative process to
canvass every eligible mail-in ballot and ensure a free, fair, and secure electoral process. Please
remember to rely on the Maryland State Board of Elections and your local election officials as your
trusted sources of information.”
Mail-In Ballot Delivery Update
The state’s mail-in ballot vendor sent replacement ballots beginning May 22 to all voters who
requested mail-in ballots prior to May 14. Each ballot packet contains detailed instructions for voting
and submitting a mail-in ballot. Additionally, impacted voters must remember to dispose of their
original ballot and to vote the replacement ballot.
Replacement ballots can be returned via drop box, at an early voting center during early voting, at a
polling place on Election Day, at a local board of elections or postmarked no later than June 23.
Locations can be found by visiting vote.md.gov/vote2026.
Additional information about Maryland’s Primary Election, including deadlines to return your voted
ballot, can be found at vote.md.gov/vote2026 or by downloading the free Go Vote Maryland! app
from the Google Play store or the Apple store.

title: More Info and Next Steps Regarding Mail In Ballots ES
text: La Junta Electoral del Estado de Maryland brinda más información y comparte los pasos a seguir con las papeletas de voto por correo ANNAPOLIS (18 de mayo de 2026) — ANNAPOLIS (18 de mayo de 2026) - Como se informó el 15 de mayo de 2026, la Junta Electoral del Estado de Maryland (SBE, por sus siglas en inglés) fue notificada sobre un error de impresión por parte del proveedor de papeletas de voto por correo para la Elección Primaria Gubernamental de Maryland 2026, programada para el 23 de junio de 2026. A continuación ofrecemos más información a los electores de Maryland y otras partes interesadas sobre los próximos pasos a seguir con las boletas de voto por correo. A partir del 9 de mayo de 2026, se comenzaron a enviar papeletas de voto por correo a todos los electores que las solicitaron antes del 6 de mayo de 2026. Aunque algunos electores pueden haber recibido la boleta correcta y la afiliación al partido que se corresponden con sus datos de registro, un error en la codificación con el proveedor de papeletas de voto por correo de la SBE provocó que algunos electores recibieran la papeleta equivocada. Debido a que el proveedor de boletas de voto por correo no pudo identificar con precisión quién recibió las boletas correctas y quién no, la SBE determinó que la única manera de garantizar la integridad y seguridad del proceso de votación por correo era enviar una nueva boleta a todos los electores que solicitaron una boleta de voto por correo. Notificación a todos los electores afectados Todos los electores que recibirán una papeleta de reemplazo recibirán una postal en la misma dirección donde reciben su papeleta.

title: Statement from Taylor Print & Visual Impressions Inc on Mail In Ballots
text:
Taylor Print & Visual Impressions, Inc.’s Statement Regarding Mail Ballot Printing Error
Taylor Print & Visual Impressions, Inc. (“TPVI”) recently became aware of an issue involving the
incorrect distribution of ballot materials in connection with a primary election mailing. Specifically, a
portion of voters received ballot packets intended for a different voter segment.
We understand the seriousness of this matter and the importance of accuracy and trust in all election-
related communications. Upon identifying the issue, we immediately began working closely with our
customer and election officials to investigate the cause, implement corrective actions, and support the
timely delivery of accurate materials to affected voters.
We have implemented additional quality control and verification measures to help prevent this type of
issue from occurring in the future.
At TPVI, we are committed to maintaining the highest standards of security, precision, and operational
integrity, and we regret the confusion this situation may have caused.
Sincerely,
The TPVI Election Services Team
Frequently Asked Questions
Is there a risk of duplicate voting because of this error?
No. There is no risk of duplicate voting as a result of this issue. Election officials have safeguards in place to
ensure that only the corrected ballots included in the replacement mailing will be accepted and counted.
When will I receive my new ballot?
Replacement ballots are currently being prepared and mailed. All ballots will be remailed by 5/29/2026.
Additional updates will be communicated by election officials as they become available.
What should I do with my original ballot?
Voters should securely discard or destroy the original ballot materials they received and use only the
replacement ballot sent in the new mailing.
Will my vote still count?
Yes. Eligible voters who complete and return their replacement ballot in accordance with election
instructions will have their vote counted.
What is being done to prevent this from happening again?
We are conducting a full review of the issue and implementing additional verification and quality control
measures to strengthen accuracy and help prevent similar situations in the future.

text:
Jared DeMarinis Michael Summers,
State Administrator
Chairman
Jim Shalleck, Vice Chair

Diane Butler
Victoria Jackson-Stanley
Eric Bryant
Maryland State Board of Elections Addresses an Error
with Mail-In Ballots
ANNAPOLIS (May 15, 2026) — The Maryland State Board of Elections has been made aware
of an error by our mail-in ballot vendor resulting in some voters receiving the wrong party ballot
for the Gubernatorial Primary Election.
In order to maintain the highest level of confidence and accuracy in mail-in voting, SBE is
working with the vendor to send replacement mail-in ballots. While it is possible only a small
number of voters received the wrong ballot, and most voters received the correct ballot, all
voters must be issued a replacement ballot. This action of resending ballots maintains the
integrity and security of mail-in voting.
This error affects only voters who were mailed a ballot before May 14, 2026. If a voter
requested and received their mail-in ballot by web delivery (Print at Home ballot), their ballot will
not be affected. All affected voters will be notified.
“We are diligently working to address this error and provide clear instructions to those affected
as quickly as possible,” said Maryland State Administrator of Elections, Jared DeMarinis. “The
State and Local Boards of Elections remain committed to running an election that is verified,
secure and accurate. Mail-in voting is an integral facet of the electoral process. With over
500,000 voters requesting mail-in ballots, we want to eliminate any doubt in its integrity or
accuracy that is why I have arranged the sending of replacement ballots.”
Mr. DeMarinis emphasized, “Please be assured that we are actively answering phones and
responding to emails and will remain transparent as we navigate through this situation. We will
make every effort to ensure that everyone affected knows the situation and how to cast their
ballot. Every vote matters, your voice will be heard, and our elections will remain verified, open,
transparent, and secure.”
SBE understands that this situation might cause the spread of misinformation. Please
remember to rely on election officials as your trusted sources for election information.
Any questions or concerns can be directed to the Maryland State Board of Elections by emailing
info.sbe@maryland.gov or calling 410-269-2840.

vote.md.gov/vote2026 or by downloading the free Go Vote Maryland! app from
the Google Play store or the Apple store.

title: Mail in Ballot Press Statement ES
text:
La Junta Electoral del Estado de Maryland 
comunica un error en las papeletas de voto por correo

ANNAPOLIS (15 de mayo de 2026) — La Junta de Electoral del Estado de Maryland ha sido informada de un error por parte del proveedor de boletas de voto por correo que resultó en que algunos electores recibieran la papeleta del partido equivocado para la Elección Primaria Gubernamental.

Con el fin de mantener la confianza y asegurar la precisión de la votación por correo, la SBE está trabajando con el proveedor para enviar boletas de voto correo de reemplazo. Aunque es posible que solo un pequeño número de electores haya recibido la papeleta incorrecta y la mayoría de los electores tengan la boleta correcta, todos los electores deben recibir una papeleta de reemplazo para votar por correo. La acción de reenviar las boletas asegura que se mantenga la integridad y la seguridad del voto por correo.

Este error solo afecta a los electores que recibieron una boleta de voto por correo antes del 14 de mayo de 2026.  No se verán afectados los electores que hayan pedido y recibido su papeleta de voto por correo con la opción de entrega web (papeleta para imprimir en casa). Se notificará a todos los electores afectados.

"Estamos trabajando intensamente para abordar este error y dar instrucciones claras a los afectados lo más rápido posible", dijo el Administrador de Elecciones del Estado de Maryland, Jared DeMarinis. "Las Juntas Electorales Estatales y Locales siguen comprometidas a llevar a cabo una elección verificada, segura y precisa. El voto por correo es una parte fundamental del proceso electoral. Tenemos más de 500,000 electores que solicitaron boletas de voto por correo, y queremos eliminar cualquier duda acerca de la integridad y precisión del voto por este medio. Por eso, he organizado el envío de papeletas de reemplazo".

El Sr. DeMarinis enfatizó: "Les aseguramos que estamos respondiendo activamente a los teléfonos y respondiendo a los correos electrónicos, y seguiremos trabajando con transparencia a medida que avancemos en esta situación.  Haremos todos los esfuerzos necesarios para asegurar que todos los afectados estén al tanto de la situación y sepan cómo emitir su voto. Cada voto importa, su voz será escuchada y nuestras elecciones seguirán siendo verificadas, abiertas, transparentes y seguras".

La SBE sabe que esta situación podría llevar a que se difunda información falsa o engañosa. Por eso les recordamos que siempre se apoyen en los funcionarios electorales como fuentes confiables de información electoral.

Cualquier pregunta o inquietud puede dirigirse a la Junta Electoral del Estado de Maryland enviando un correo electrónico a info.sbe@maryland.gov o llamando al 410-269-2840.

Encuentre más información sobre la Elección Primaria de Maryland en vote.md.gov/vote2026 o descargando la aplicación gratuita Go Vote Maryland! de la tienda Google Play o la tienda Apple.

title: SBE Judges and Election Pages
text:
Jared DeMarinis Michael Summers,
State Administrator
Chairman
Jim Shalleck, Vice Chair
Katherine Berry
Deputy Administrator
Diane Butler
Victoria Jackson-Stanley
Eric Bryant
Maryland State Board of Elections Encourages Marylanders
to Explore the Benefits of Serving as Election Judges and
Election Pages
ANNAPOLIS (May 12, 2026) — The Maryland State Board of Elections (SBE) is calling on
eligible Marylanders to take part in the 2026 Primary Election by serving as election judges and
election pages.
There are several benefits to serving as an election judge. Eligible Marylanders aged 16 and
older can earn money and help other residents cast their votes by serving as election judges.
Those who have previously served as an Election Judge are eligible for a one-time $100 bonus
payment. Election judges check in voters, provide guidance and answer questions, and help
oversee a smooth voting experience. To apply to be an election judge, use SBE’s online form or
contact your local Board of Elections. It is vital to SBE operations to have an adequate number
of Election Judges on call, in the event that there are last minute cancellations and to help begin
recruitment for the 2026 General Election cycle.
Additionally, eligible 14-15-year-olds can serve as Election Day Pages. Pages are student
volunteers who, under the direction of Chief Election Judges, assist Election Judges and voters
on Election Day. To become an Election Day Page, apply using our online form or contact
your local Board of Elections. Serving as an election page also provides students with an
opportunity to earn service-learning credit hours for school.
“Election judges and pages are essential to the success of Maryland’s elections and the
strength of our democratic process,” said State Administrator Jared DeMarinis. “Their service
helps ensure every voter can cast a ballot confidently and that every vote is counted accurately,
fairly, and securely. Election judges also play a crucial role in maintaining the integrity and
security of elections across the state. For younger Marylanders, serving as an election page
offers a unique and rewarding introduction to the election process and civic engagement. I
encourage all eligible Marylanders to consider serving their communities as election judges or
election pages and help protect the voting rights of their fellow citizens.”
State of Maryland employees and county government employees who are scheduled to be an
election judge can earn administrative leave . Be sure to check with your employer for any
added benefits of serving as an election judge.
Please remember to rely on your state and local government election officials as your
trusted sources for election information. Additional information about Maryland’s
Primary Election can be found at vote.md.gov/vote2026 or by downloading the free
Go Vote Maryland! app from the Google Play store or the Apple store.

text: La Junta Electoral del Estado de Maryland anima a los habitantes del estado a informarse sobre los beneficios de ser jueces y asistentes electorales ANNAPOLIS (12 de mayo de 2026) — La Junta Electoral del Estado de Maryland (SBE) extiende un llamado a los residentes de Maryland elegibles para que participen en las elecciones primarias de 2026 sirviendo como jueces y asistentes electorales. Ser trabajador electoral tiene varios beneficios. Los habitantes de Maryland de 16 años o más que sean elegibles pueden ganar dinero y ayudar a votar a otros electores participando de las elecciones como jueces electorales. Si ya fue Juez Electoral en otras elecciones, será elegible para un pago único de $100 en concepto de bonificación. Los trabajadores electorales registran a los electores, los guían, responden preguntas y ayudan a que tengan una experiencia de voto sin complicaciones. Para aplicar para ser Juez Electoral, use el formulario en línea de SBE o comuníquese con su Junta Electoral local. Contar con un número adecuado de Jueces Electorales de guardia es de vital importancia para el trabajo de la SBE en caso de que se produzcan cancelaciones de última hora, y también para ayudar a comenzar el reclutamiento para el ciclo electoral general de 2026. Además, los jóvenes elegibles de 14 a 15 años pueden servir como asistentes en el día de las elecciones. Los asistentes son estudiantes voluntarios que, bajo la dirección de los Jueces Electorales Principales, ayudan a los Jueces Electorales y a los votantes el Día de las Elecciones. Para ser asistente en el día de las elecciones, puede aplicar con nuestro formulario en línea o contactar a su junta electoral local.

title: SBE Judges and Election Pages ES

Ser asistente en las elecciones también les permite a los estudiantes la oportunidad de ganar horas de crédito de aprendizaje-servicio para la escuela. "Los jueces y los asistentes electorales son esenciales para el éxito de las elecciones de Maryland y para mantener la fortaleza de nuestro proceso democrático", dijo el administrador estatal Jared DeMarinis. "Su trabajo ayuda a garantizar que cada elector pueda emitir su voto con confianza y que cada voto se cuente de manera precisa, justa y segura. Los trabajadores electorales también desempeñan un papel crucial en para mantener la integridad y la seguridad de las elecciones en todo el estado. Para los jóvenes de Maryland, participar como asistentes electorales les ofrece una forma única y gratificante de ingresar al proceso electoral y comprometerse con el deber cívico. Les pido a todos los habitantes de Maryland elegibles que consideren servir a sus comunidades como jueces o asistentes electorales y ayuden a proteger los derechos de voto de sus conciudadanos". Diane Butler
Katherine Berry

Eric Bryant
Maryland State Board of Elections Announces 565,639 Voters
Have Requested Mail-In Ballots for the 2026 Primary Election
First Phase of Ballot Mailings Will Be Mailed by Monday, May 11
ANNAPOLIS (May 5, 2026) — The Maryland State Board of Elections today announced
that 565,639 voters have already requested mail-in ballots for the 2026 Primary Election. The SBE
will begin transmitting Primary Election Ballots to voters who are eligible to vote in the primary
election and requested a ballot in advance by Monday, May 11. For ballots sent by mail, it is
expected that voters will receive their ballot within five days.
There is still time to request a mail-in ballot. To receive a ballot via mail or fax, your request must be
received (not just mailed) or submitted online by Tuesday, June 16. To receive your mail-in ballot via
email, submit your request online no later than Friday, June 19.
To ensure the secure transmittal of mail-in ballots, voters can verify that their local board of elections
received their mail-in ballot request and can track the status of their ballot by visiting SBE’s voter
look-up website. If you want to receive and vote a mail-in ballot for all future Federal and State
elections, sign up for the permanent mail-in ballot list using the mail-in ballot application.
“Voters who want to utilize mail-in ballots should request their ballot early to ensure you have plenty
of time to return your voted ballot,” said Jared DeMarinis, State Administrator of Elections. “Mail-in
ballots are convenient, secure, and trusted method of voting. Maryland employs tracking technology
on the ballots ensuring confidence in the integrity of mail-in voting. Remember that ballot drop boxes
are a great way to return your mail-in ballot.”
To return your voted mail-in ballot, the ballot must be postmarked by or before 8 p.m. on Election
Day, Tuesday, June 23. If returned by hand, ballots must be dropped at a secure ballot drop box or
local board of elections by 8 p.m. on Tuesday, June 23.
Please remember to rely on your state and local government election officials as your trusted
sources for election information. Additional information about Maryland’s Primary Election, including
deadlines to return your voted ballot, can be found at vote.md.gov/vote2026 or by downloading the
free Go Vote Maryland! app from the Google Play store or the Apple store.

text:
La Junta Electoral del Estado de Maryland anuncia que 565,639 electores solicitaron boletas de voto por correo para las elecciones primarias de 2026
La primera fase de los envíos de papeletas por correo postal será antes del lunes 11 de mayo

Annapolis, MD (5 de mayo de 2026) — Hoy, la Junta Electoral del Estado de Maryland (SBE) anunció que 565,639 votantes ya han solicitado boletas de voto por correo para las elecciones primarias de 2026. A partir del 11 de mayo, la SBE comenzará a enviar las boletas para las elecciones primarias a los electores que puedan votar y que hayan pedido una boleta con anticipación. Se espera que las boletas que se envían por correo postal lleguen al domicilio de los electores en los cinco días siguientes.

Todavía hay tiempo para pedir una boleta de voto por correo. Si quiere recibir su boleta de voto por correo por correo postal o por fax, la solicitud tiene que recibirse (no solo enviarse) por internet o por correo postal hasta el martes 16 de junio. Para recibir su papeleta por correo electrónico, envíe su solicitud por internet a más tardar el viernes 19 de junio.

Para garantizar el envío seguro de las papeletas de voto por correo, los electores pueden verificar que su junta electoral local haya recibido la solicitud de boleta de voto por correo y pueden rastrear el estado de la boleta en el sitio web de búsqueda de electores de SBE. Si desea recibir una boleta y votar por correo en todas las próximas elecciones federales y estatales, inscríbase en la lista de boletas permanentes por correo utilizando la solicitud de papeletas de voto por correo.

"Los electores que quieran utilizar boletas de voto por correo deben pedir su boleta anticipadamente para asegurarse de tener suficiente tiempo para devolver la boleta con su voto", dijo Jared DeMarinis, Administrador Estatal de Elecciones. "Las boletas de voto por correo son un método de votación conveniente, seguro y confiable. Maryland usa tecnología de seguimiento en las boletas, lo que le garantiza la confianza en la integridad de la votación por correo. Recuerde que los buzones electorales son una excelente manera de devolver su boleta de voto por correo".

Cuando devuelva la boleta de voto por correo después de completarla, debe tener matasellos antes de las 8 p.m. del día de las elecciones, martes 23 de junio. Si se devuelven en persona, las boletas deben depositarse en un buzón electoral seguro o en la junta electoral local antes de las 8 p.m. del martes 23 de junio.

Siempre confíe en los funcionarios electorales del gobierno estatal y local sus fuentes confiables de información electoral. Puede encontrar más información sobre la Elección Primaria de Maryland, como las fechas límite para entregar la papeleta cuando la complete, en vote.md.gov/vote2026 o descargando la aplicación gratuita Go Vote Maryland! de la tienda Google Play o la tienda Apple.

Maryland State Board of Elections Reminds Marylanders of
Voter Registration Options
ANNAPOLIS (April 28, 2026) As the 2026 primary election approaches, the Maryland State Board
of Elections (SBE) reminds residents of their voter registration options and deadlines.
"Maryland is at its strongest when residents make their voices heard in our electoral process, and
that starts with registering to vote,” said SBE Administrator Jared DeMarinis. “By registering early
and making a plan to vote, Marylanders take an active role in shaping the future through our
democratic process."
How to Register to Vote
There are three ways to register to vote in this year’s elections.
Register Online: The preliminary deadline to register or update voter registration is Tuesday, June
2. To register online, use SBE’s online registration system.
Register by Mail: Residents can register by printing the registration form (English version and
Spanish version) and mailing it by June 2. Mailed registrations must be postmarked by this date.
Alternatively, residents can submit it at their local board of elections.
Register In-Person: Residents can register during Early Voting from Thursday, June 11 to
Thursday, June 18, or on Primary Election Day, Tuesday, June 23. Polls are open from 7 a.m. to 8
p.m. Voters in line by 8 p.m. will be able to register. A list of early voting locations will be posted
online. Make sure to bring a document that proves where you live when you attempt to vote at your
local polling place or early voting center.
Learn more about Maryland’s Primary Election at vote.md.gov/vote2026 or by downloading the free
Go Vote Maryland! app from the Google Play store or the Apple store.

La Junta Electoral del Estado de Maryland les recuerda a los electores qué opciones tienen para registrarse

Annapolis, MD (28 de abril de 2026) — Mientras se acercan las elecciones primarias de 2026, la Junta Electoral del Estado de Maryland (SBE) les recuerda a los electores las opciones y plazos para registrarse.

"El momento en que Maryland se siente más fuerte es cuando los habitantes hacen oír su voz durante el proceso electoral, y eso comienza con cuando se registran para votar", dijo el administrador de SBE, Jared DeMarinis. "Registrarse lo antes posible y tener un plan para votar permite que los habitantes de Maryland tengan un rol activo a la hora de darle forma a nuestro futuro a través del proceso democrático".

Cómo registrarse para votar

Hay tres formas de registrarse para votar en las elecciones de este año.

Regístrese por internet: La fecha límite preliminar para registrarse o actualizar el registro de votantes es el martes 2 de junio. Para registrarse por internet, use el sistema de registro en línea de SBE.

Regístrese por correo: Los electores pueden inscribirse imprimiendo el formulario de inscripción (versión en inglés y versión en español) y enviándolo por correo antes del 2 de junio. Los registros enviados por correo postal deben tener matasellos de hasta esa fecha. Si lo desean, los residentes tienen la opción de enviarlo a la junta electoral local.

Registrarse en persona: Los residentes pueden registrarse durante la votación anticipada del jueves 11 al jueves 18 de junio, o el día de las elecciones primarias, martes 23 de junio. Las urnas están abiertas de 7 a.m. a 8 p.m. Los electores que estén en fila antes de las 8 p.m. podrán registrarse. La lista completa de lugares de votación anticipada será publicada eninternet. Si va a registrarse el día en que vota, tiene que llevar un documento que demuestre donde vive cuando vaya a votar a su centro de votación local o al centro de votación anticipada.

Puede encontrar más información sobre la Elección Primaria de Maryland en vote.md.gov/vote2026 o descargando la aplicación gratuita Go Vote Maryland! de la tienda Google Play o la tienda Apple.

text: Jared DeMarinis Michael Summers, Chairman State Administrator Jim Shalleck, Vice Chair Diane Butler Katherine Berry Victoria Jackson-Stanley Deputy Administrator Eric Bryant Maryland State Board of Elections Highlights Voting Options and Deadlines for the 2026 Primary Election ANNAPOLIS (April 7, 2026) — With the 2026 Primary Election approaching, the Maryland State Board of Elections (SBE) today shared with Marylanders a comprehensive guide to the primary election’s key dates and voting options. To ensure every voice is heard, SBE is highlighting three convenient ways to exercise your right to vote, along with the critical deadlines to help voters plan. “An informed electorate is the foundation of a successful election,” said State Administrator Jared DeMarinis. “Whether you choose to vote by mail, cast your vote at an early voting center, or head to the polls on Primary Election Day, we want every Marylander to have the information they need to cast their ballot with confidence.” Three Ways to Cast Your Ballot Marylanders can choose one of three voting methods: 1. Early Voting In-Person Avoid the Election Day rush by voting early. Dates: Thursday, June 11 through Thursday, June 18 Hours: 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. daily. Note: If you are in line by 8 p.m. you will be permitted to cast a ballot. A complete list of early voting centers is available online (Spanish version). 2. Mail-In Voting: Voters who prefer to vote by mail should take note of the following application deadlines: • By Mail or Fax: Requests to receive a mail-in ballot by mail or fax must be received (not postmarked) by Tuesday, June 16. • By Email: Requests to receive a mail-in ballot via email must be submitted by 11:59 p.m. on Friday, June 19. • Submitting Your Ballot: Completed ballots must be postmarked by Tuesday, June 23.

title: SBE Key Primary Dates
text: If returning by hand, ballots must be deposited into an official ballot drop box or delivered to your local board of elections by 8 p.m. on Primary Election Day, Tuesday, June 23. Find ballot drop box locations at vote.md.gov/vote2026. 3. Election Day In-Person The third option is to vote in person at your local polling place on Primary Election Day, Tuesday, June 23. • Hours: Polls are open from 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. • Location: Voters must report to their assigned polling place. You can locate your polling place on the SBE website (English and Spanish). title: GoVote App Released
text:
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE

The Maryland State Board of Elections announces the launch of their voter resource phone app, Go Vote Maryland!

Annapolis, MD (March 25, 2026) — The Maryland State Board of Elections is excited to announce the launch of their voter resource phone app, Go Vote Maryland!  Go Vote MD was developed through a collaborative effort involving researchers and students from the Empowering Secure Elections research lab Towson University and the Center for Democracy and Civic Engagement at the University of Maryland, in partnership with the Maryland State Board of Elections.  The free app is now available for download on the Google Play store and the Apple store.

The Go Vote Maryland! app aims to be the voter’s new go-to source for election information! The app was designed to help voters easily access important, trusted information right at their fingertips.  On the app, voters can view the election calendar, report misinformation, find their voting location, check their voter registration, get answers to frequently asked questions and more.

“We’re excited about the release of this app. The app will be an invaluable tool helping voters access pertinent information to use their voice in the upcoming election,” said Jared DeMarinis, State Administrator of Elections. “The Maryland State Board of Elections continues to prioritize voter outreach, voter education and election transparency. This app is another tool in our mission to ensure elections are verified, open, transparent and empowering.”

Please remember to rely on your state and local government election officials as your trusted sources for election information.  Visit SBE’s website, follow SBE on social media, download our new app, Go Vote Maryland, or contact your local elections office for accurate election information. Report any suspicious information to SBE’s disinformation portal.

title: Gambling on Elections
text:
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE

The Maryland State Board of Elections Uses National Problem Gambling Awareness Month to Educate the Public on an Important Topic

Annapolis, MD (March 20, 2026) — March is National Problem Gambling Awareness Month. While the State Board of Elections takes no position on gambling or iGaming, it is important to inform the public regarding wagering on the outcome of Maryland elections.

Gambling on elections is illegal in Maryland. A person may not make a bet or wager on election results. Unlike sports betting, which is regulated and permitted through licensed operators, betting on elections is not authorized and falls outside the scope of legal gambling activities. Maryland law is designed to protect the integrity and public trust of the electoral processes. Engaging in election-related wagering within the State could expose individuals to legal penalties.

Despite this prohibition, some platforms, known as prediction markets, operate in a limited, regulated capacity at the federal level. These platforms are structured differently from traditional gambling sites and are framed as “forecasting” rather than betting. These platforms allow users to trade contracts based on the outcomes of events, including elections.

It is important for Maryland residents to understand that even though such platforms are accessible online, participation may still conflict with state law. Users should exercise caution and stay informed about both state and federal regulations before engaging with any prediction market involving elections. At best, engaging in these election prediction markets goes against the spirit and intent of the prohibition and at worst, it is wagering on electoral outcomes and carries criminal and civil penalties.

Again, the integrity of elections must be preserved. Financial incentives should not influence or appear to influence election results. Artificial online markets don’t determine electoral outcomes; only voters using their voice can determine electoral outcomes.

Please remember to rely on your state and local government election officials as your trusted sources for election information. title: US Dept of Homeland Security Elections Release
text: Jared DeMarinis Michael Summers, State Administrator Chairman Jim Shalleck, Vice Katherine Berry Deputy Administrator Chairman Diane Butler Victoria Jackson- Stanley Eric Bryant FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE State Administrator of Elections addresses recent statements regarding the role of the US Department of Homeland Security and elections Annapolis, MD (February 18, 2026) — Recent high profile press statements have suggested the possibility of the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) running elections in an attempt to cast doubts on election security and integrity by the States. Before any misinformation or disinformation takes hold from these statements, the State Administrator of Elections Jared DeMarinis issued the following statement to provide corrective information. The law is clear: in the event of a state of emergency that interferes with the electoral process, the Governor of Maryland has the authority, not FEMA, to mandate any changes. FEMA cannot close polling places, alter the election date or change how or the manner we vote. Furthermore, if an emergency circumstance occurs but not a state of emergency, the State Board may petition the circuit court to take remedial actions in the public interest and to protect the integrity of the electoral process. Again, the authority rests with the State, not FEMA. The President, DHS or FEMA has no constitutional or statutory authority to take over Maryland’s elections and electoral processes during a state of emergency or emergency circumstances. Once again, Maryland’s voter registration process and integrity have been called into question especially with regard to citizenship. As State Administrator of Elections, I want to reassure all Marylanders that the Maryland State Board of Elections (SBE) and our local election officials are unwavering in their commitment to maintaining an accurate, secure, and trustworthy voter registration list, fully compliant with both federal and State laws.

title: US Dept of Homeland Security Elections Release
text: As State Administrator of Elections, I want to reassure all Marylanders that the Maryland State Board of Elections (SBE) and our local election officials are unwavering in their commitment to maintaining an accurate, secure, and trustworthy voter registration list, fully compliant with both federal and State laws. As State Administrator, I am legally charged with maintaining the accuracy and currency of the statewide voter registration list. This is a responsibility I do not take lightly. It is a privilege and honor to safeguard the right to vote. Public trust in the electoral process is paramount. It is the bedrock of our democracy and the foundation for any elected government. Voter registration list maintenance is not a static process. It is a daily effort with continuous updates and changes. In respect to citizenship updates, Maryland law sets forth two specific instances where SBE can act on information about potential noncitizens. The Administrative Office of the Court (AOC) sends SBE information about potential jurors who indicated they did not qualify for jury service because they were not a U.S. citizen, and SBE also accepts self- reporting directly from individuals. Before any individual is removed from the statewide voter registration list based on an AOC report, SBE verifies the information by sending a written notification to the individual requesting confirmation of their citizenship status. FAX (410) 974- 2019 Toll Free Phone Number (800) 222-8683 151 West Street Suite 200 MD Relay Service (800) 735-2258 https://elections.maryland.gov Annapolis, Maryland 21401 If information is received from a third party source regarding citizenship status of a registered voter, that information cannot be confirmed by SBE.

title: US Dept of Homeland Security Elections Release
text: FAX (410) 974- 2019 Toll Free Phone Number (800) 222-8683 151 West Street Suite 200 MD Relay Service (800) 735-2258 https://elections.maryland.gov Annapolis, Maryland 21401 If information is received from a third party source regarding citizenship status of a registered voter, that information cannot be confirmed by SBE. Since SBE cannot take any administrative action to remove or cancel the individual based upon these third party reports, SBE forwards that information to the Office of the State Prosecutor (OSP) for further investigation. Maryland's detailed and legally circumscribed process for removing a voter from the registration list is designed to be absolutely certain and remove any doubt in the cancellation. Without the necessary verification steps required by State law, election officials cannot cancel a voter registration record. This office will not disenfranchise a voter based upon partial or unsubstantiated evidence. The right to vote is a sacred right that has been expanded through the sacrifices of many before us. Maryland does not want to erect artificial barriers in registering to vote or voting, nor does it want you to re-register to vote due to an improper or illegal cancellation. Remember voting is not an entitlement nor benefit program created or established by the government, but a constitutional right embedded in the principles of our nation’s foundation, our Constitution and the Maryland Declaration of Rights. Regarding the issue of SAVE (Systemic Alien Verification for Entitlements) and the possibility of mandating its use for verification of citizenship in the voter registration process, Maryland does not use the United States Citizenship and Immigration Services' (USCIS) SAVE database in the voter registration or list maintenance processes. SAVE isn’t designed and purposed for voter registration nor to assist in maintaining voter roll accuracy. Additionally, Maryland law does not provide SAVE as a permissible means for list maintenance.

title: US Dept of Homeland Security Elections Release
text: SAVE isn’t designed and purposed for voter registration nor to assist in maintaining voter roll accuracy. Additionally, Maryland law does not provide SAVE as a permissible means for list maintenance. Furthermore, the SAVE database has been reported to produce erroneous information about registered voters’ citizenship. Using SAVE could disenfranchise qualified voters. This is contrary to the intent of Maryland law that ensures the maximum number of eligible individuals can register rather than disenfranchising eligible individuals with unnecessary burdens to exercising their constitutional right to vote. The State Administrator and SBE staff oversee our cybersecurity defensive efforts against bad actors, not the federal government or CISA (Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency). Our security team is an integral part of our daily operations and public facing voter services ensuring the highest levels of awareness and preparedness. Periodic updates on our security posture are presented to the bipartisan State Board members. Moreover, SBE works closely and collaboratively with our State partners as well as other states for sharing alerts on possible cyberthreats. This collaboration does not impair nor undermine our independence and nonpartisan mission. Finally, every eligible Marylander is the right person to vote. Their voice will determine who will govern our State. Elections from all the votes cast decide the right leaders for Maryland’s future. And every vote cast is counted. As our Declaration of Rights states so distinctly and clearly: “the right of the People to participate in the Legislature is the best security of liberty and the foundation of all free Government; . . . and every citizen having the qualifications prescribed by the Constitution, ought to have the right of suffrage.” As I stated before, Marylanders should feel confident in our election administration.

title: US Dept of Homeland Security Elections Release
text: Always verify the information you hear or see whether on social media, from a friend, or any other source with the trusted source of electoral information, the Maryland State Board of Elections. SBE ensures Marylanders can exercise their constitutional right in a verified, open, transparent and empowering manner that is safe and secure. For more information visit www.elections.maryland.gov . ### Media Contacts: Bruce Miller, bmiller@kopublicaffairs.com 410-916-6951 Lexy Rhoden, morgan.rhoden@maryland.gov 443-924-1644

title: MD State Administrator of Elections Addresses MisDisinformation of Nationalization of Elections
text: Jared DeMarinis Michael Summers, State Administrator Chairman Jim Shalleck, Vice Katherine Berry Deputy Administrator Chairman Diane Butler Victoria Jackson- Stanley Eric Bryant FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE The Maryland State Administrator of Elections Addresses Mis/Disinformation of the “Nationalization of Elections” Annapolis, MD (February 6, 2026) — Recent events and high-profile press statements have suggested the possibility of nationalizing election administration in an attempt to cast doubts on election security maintained by the States. Before any misinformation or disinformation takes hold from these statements, the State Administrator of Elections, Jared DeMarinis, issued the following statement to provide corrective information: The United States Constitution is clear: the authority to administer elections predominately resides with the States. The States administer and conduct elections each according to their laws and regulations, subject to limited Congressional authority. The President of the United States has no constitutional or statutory authority to nationalize Maryland’s elections and electoral processes. As State Administrator of the Maryland State Board of Elections, I want to assure voters that we are dedicated to ensuring that all elections are run in a manner that is safe, secure, transparent and accessible for all eligible voters. We are guided by the principle enshrined in Maryland’s Declaration of Rights- “the right of the People to participate in the Legislature is the best security of liberty and the foundation of all free Government; . . . and every citizen having the qualifications prescribed by the Constitution, ought to have the right of suffrage.” Additionally, statements on the presence of federal enforcement agents in and around polling locations may cause apprehension or anxiety for certain communities. This office is committed to protecting voters from undue harassment or intimidation regarding when they voted, how they voted, and who they voted for.

title: MD State Administrator of Elections Addresses MisDisinformation of Nationalization of Elections
text: This office is committed to protecting voters from undue harassment or intimidation regarding when they voted, how they voted, and who they voted for. Elections are the foundation of our democracy, and, in 2026, it is how we use our voice to determine the future of our State. Mail-in voting is a viable option and an alternative to in-person voting. Mail-in voting is safe, secure, convenient and legal. Don’t let the noise disenfranchise or silence your voice. This right was hard fought for over the course of our country’s history, and we do not take protecting that right lightly. title: MSBE Launches Modernized Campaign Finance Reporting Systems
text:
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE
Maryland State Board of Elections Launches Modernized
Campaign Finance Reporting Systems to Strengthen
Transparency and Efficiency
Annapolis, MD (January 12, 2026) — The Maryland State Board of Elections
(SBE) today announced the launch of its upgraded Maryland Campaign
Reporting Information System (MD-CRIS) and Business Contribution Disclosure
System (BCDS), delivering a major modernization in campaign finance
disclosure, data accuracy, and public transparency.
The new MD-CRIS and BCDS platforms enhance how candidates, committees,
and businesses report campaign-related financial activity, while offering Maryland
voters faster, clearer, and more comprehensive access to the information that
supports free and fair elections.
“These new systems represent a significant step forward in strengthening
Maryland’s framework for transparency, accountability, and efficient campaign
finance administration,” said Jared DeMarinis, State Administrator, Maryland
State Board of Elections. “With real-time visibility, improved data accuracy,
automated compliance tools, and easier public access, we are ensuring that our
election processes remain secure, modern, and voter-focused.”
To support Maryland’s long-standing commitment to election integrity, the new
systems were designed with both the public and filers in mind. They deliver
improved accuracy and streamlined reporting for committees and businesses,
while giving residents faster access to campaign finance information through a
more transparent and user-friendly platform. The system upgrades improve staff
efficiency and compliance oversight, reinforcing Maryland’s leadership in election
administration and public accountability.

Specifically, the new systems will deliver a number of key benefits, including:
Enhancing Public Trust and Accountability
• Real-time visibility into reported financial transactions
• Public portal ensuring full access to all filed data
• Faster public searches with enhanced analytical database technology
Improving Efficiency and Data Quality
• Guided data entry improves accuracy and prevents incomplete filings
• Automated calculations reduce reporting errors and manual work
Streamlining User Experience
• Clear, intuitive filing process and visuals to understand financial data
• Simplified committee registration with modern guided steps
Technical and Administrative Advantages
• Automated compliance checks and business rules support auditing
• Standardized notifications and self-service tools reduce administrative
workload
• Fast, modern processing architecture with automated error files for
imports
“Maryland’s commitment to innovation in election administration continues to
ensure voters have confidence in our democratic process,” added DeMarinis.
“These platforms are built not only to serve campaigns and committees, but to
strengthen the public’s trust in the integrity and transparency of our elections.”
For more information visit www.elections.maryland.gov .
###

title: USPS Policy Change Press Release
text:
Maryland State Board of Elections Reassures Voters that Mail-in
Voting is a Secure and Convenient Option for Casting Your Vote
ANNAPOLIS, MD (January 14, 2026) - Amidst new United States Postal Services (USPS)
policy changes, the Maryland State Board of Elections (SBE) wants to remind voters that
mail-in voting remains a safe, convenient and effective way to vote.
USPS proposed a new rule, Postmarks and Postal Possession, 90 FR 38716, effective
December 25, 2025. This new language was intended to provide clarity on postmarks and
their relationship to the date of mailing. The rule advises that, due to postal operations, the
postmark date does not always correspond to the date on which the Postal Service first
accepted possession.
“I urge every voter who wants to cast a mail-in ballot with USPS to act early or to utilize one
of our 286 ballot drop boxes. Ballot drop boxes are located throughout the State to ensure
equal access for all voters. Each ballot drop box is routinely emptied, well lit, and under
surveillance to ensure safety and prevent any tampering.” said Jared DeMarinis, State
Administrator of Elections. “Mail-in voting remains a secure and convenient option for
casting your vote. Remember that the State Board of Elections is the trusted source of
information for elections and mail-in voting. Please don’t let the new rule on postmarks
disenfranchise you, make a plan for voting.”
Mail-in ballots returned by mail must be postmarked by or before 8 p.m. on Election Day,
Tuesday, June 23. If returned by hand, ballots must be dropped at a ballot drop box or local
board of elections by 8 p.m. on Tuesday, June 23.
To receive a mail-in ballot by mail, your request must be received (not just mailed) by June
16. The deadline to request a web delivery mail-in ballot is June 19. Visit SBE’s mail-in
ballot webpage for more information on how to request a ballot.
For registered voters who do not want to cast a mail-in ballot, there are two other ways to
vote in the upcoming election: vote early in-person or vote on Election Day.
Vote Early In-Person: Early voting begins Thursday, June 11 and runs through Thursday,
June 18. Early voting centers are open from 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. Find the list of early voting
centers here.
Vote on Election Day: To find your Election Day polling place, visit SBE’s Find My Polling
Place portal. Election Day polling places will be open June 23 from 7 a.m. to 8 p.m.

Please remember to rely on your state and local government election officials as your
trusted sources for election information. Visit SBE’s website, follow SBE on social media,
or contact your local elections office for accurate election information. Report any
suspicious information to SBE’s disinformation portal.

title: Election Worker - Program Overview
text: Election Worker - Program Overview What is an Election Worker Election Workers are registered Maryland voters who volunteer to assist voters during elections. About 4,000 volunteers are needed for each election. They assist in safeguarding integrity of the process and to ensure the fair and efficient operation of in-person voting at 14 early voting centers and 231election day polling places in Montgomery County. They also help collect and count ballots cast by mail, at nursing homes, or placed in drop boxes. Election Worker Roles There are different roles you can volunteer for: - Election Judges - Assist in facilitating in-person voting during Early Voting or on Election Day - Drop Box Runners – Pick up mail-in ballots from drop boxes - Canvassers – Help count mail-in ballots - Nursing Home Program Participants – Help voters in designated nursing homes Some service positions are all day, and others are part of the day. Some positions require experience or a car. View a complete list of all Early Voting and Election Day Roles Page Sections - What Is An Election Worker? - Qualifications - ADA Statement - Bilingual Election Workers and the Voting Rights Act - Election Worker Code of Conduct - Election Worker Training - Apply to be an Election Worker/Election Judge - Inclement Weather Policy and Emergency Notifications via Alert Montgomery - Election Worker Contact Information Qualifications To participate you must: - Be a U.S. citizen and registered to vote in Maryland. - Be 16 years or older.

title: Election Worker - Program Overview
text: If you are under 18, you will need a signed Permission slip . - Successfully complete all training. - Not be legally prohibited from entering onto the property of a school or being near children. - Speak, read, and write English clearly. - Not be a campaign manager or campaign treasurer - Not currently holding or running for elected office. - Be able to work the full hours of your assigned role. - Be able to lift about 25 pounds with help - Be kind and patient with voters and fellow volunteers. Election Worker Code of Conduct To ensure that Montgomery County citizens are provided with the best election experience, we ask that Election Workers adhere to the Election Worker Code of Conduct (COC) which governs individual responsibilities and polling place behavior. Violation of the Codes of Conduct may result in removal from the Montgomery County Election Worker program. The Code of Conduct will be reviewed and signed in training. Election Workers must follow the Code of Conduct. You will learn about these rules and sign them during training. Violation of the Codes of Conduct may result in removal from the Election Worker Program Bilingual Election Workers Every polling place must have one (1) volunteer bilingual in Spanish to help voters, as required by law (Voting Rights Act, Section 203). Besides volunteers who speak Spanish, we also need volunteers who speak Chinese, Korean, Vietnamese, French and other languages to help voters who request language assistance when voting. Stipend and Returning Bonus Election Workers receive a stipend for their training and service based on their position. To get paid, you must: - Provide your full Social Security Number. - Successfully complete all training. - Fulfill assigned election duties.

title: Election Worker - Program Overview
text: Stipend and Returning Bonus Election Workers receive a stipend for their training and service based on their position. To get paid, you must: - Provide your full Social Security Number. - Successfully complete all training. - Fulfill assigned election duties. If you served as an Election Judge in 2024, you will receive a bonus in 2026: - $100 for each full day served at a polling place. - $50 for each part day served at a polling place. - If you last served in the 2022 election (or earlier) or served in 2024 as a Canvasser, Drop Box Runner, or were a Nursing Home Program participant, you are not eligible to receive a bonus in 2026. ADA Statement All training locations and voting places in Montgomery County are accessible. If you need accommodations or have questions, a Board of Elections recruiter can assist you. Election Worker Training You are required to complete training to serve . - Election Judges - Complete an online training, take a quiz, and attend an in-person training class for their specific assigned position (s) - Canvassers – Attend an in-person training class before you start - Nursing Home Program Participants – Attend an in-person training class before you start - Drop Box Runners – Attend an in-person training class at the Board of Elections. You will also visit a drop box to learn proper procedures. Ready to Apply? You can apply any time, but if you want to volunteer to serve in a specific election, apply today! Complete your online application.

title: Supreme Court Upholds Maryland Mail In Ballot Law
text:
Jared DeMarinis Michael Summers,
State Administrator
Chairman
Jim Shalleck, Vice Chair
Katherine Berry
Deputy Administrator
Diane Butler
Victoria Jackson-Stanley
Eric Bryant
The Supreme Court Upholds Maryland’s Mail-In Ballot
Law Among Other States
Annapolis (June 29, 2026) - Today the Maryland State Board of Elections is excited to
share that the U.S. Supreme Court has issued a ruling in Watson v. Republican
National Committee that upholds states’ authority to process mail-in ballots received
after Election Day provided that the ballots are timely postmarked by Election Day. This
ruling safeguards mail-in ballot voters from potentially being disenfranchised from
federal elections.
Mail-in ballots are considered timely if they are postmarked on or before Election Day or
there is a proper date on the voter’s oath, and the ballots are received by 10 a.m. on the
second Friday after the Election Day.
Jared DeMarinis, State Administrator of Elections, states “this law protects the rights of
mail-in voters to make informed choices up to and including Election Day. Voters can
cast their mail-in ballots confidentially in the upcoming General Election knowing there
will be no changes to Maryland’s law regarding receiving mail-in ballots.”
Please remember to rely on your state and local government election officials as your
trusted sources for election information. Additional information about Maryland’s
Elections can be found at elections.maryland.gov or by downloading the free Go Vote
Maryland! app from the Google Play store or the Apple store.

title: SBE Canvass Resumes Primary
text:
Jared DeMarinis Michael Summers, Chairman
State Administrator
Jim Shalleck, Vice Chair
Diane Butler
Katherine Berry
Victoria Jackson-Stanley
Deputy Administrator
Eric Bryant
Post-Election Canvassing of Mail-In Ballots
Scheduled for June 25
Members of the Public May Observe the Canvass at Local Boards of Elections
ANNAPOLIS (June 24, 2026) — Maryland’s post-election canvass of mail-in ballots for the
Gubernatorial Primary Election will begin on Thursday, June 25. Local boards of elections will be
opening, reviewing, and counting mail-in ballots that have been returned. Members of the public may
observe the canvass.
“Watching democracy in action is inspiring, so we remind members of the public they may observe
the canvass at their local board of elections,” said State Elections Administrator Jared DeMarinis.
“Maryland’s canvass process is open, transparent, and conducted in compliance with all relevant laws
and regulations. I want to thank all our boards of canvassers and bipartisan canvass teams for
working tirelessly to count every vote, and ensure every vote counts.”
Local boards post on their websites the dates, times and locations of their canvasses. For more
information about a local board’s canvassing timeline, please contact the local board. To learn more
about the vote canvassing process in Maryland, visit SBE’s canvassing webpage.
The local boards will release results each day they count ballots after election day. SBE posts the
results to its website as they are received.

text:
Jared DeMarinis Michael Summers, Chairman

Tomorrow is Election Day for Maryland’s
Gubernatorial Primary Election
Voters in Line at Polling Places by 8 p.m. Can Cast a Ballot
Tomorrow is Also the Deadline to Return a Mail-In Ballot
ANNAPOLIS (June 22, 2026) — The Maryland State Board of Elections (SBE) reminds voters that
Maryland’s Gubernatorial Primary Election Day is tomorrow, June 23, 2026.
Polling places will be open from 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. Tuesday. Voters in line by 8 p.m. can cast a ballot.
A list of polling places is available online at vote.md.gov/vote2026.
Tomorrow is the also deadline to return a mail-in ballot. There are two ways to return your mail-in
ballot. Mail-in ballots returned by mail must be postmarked by or before June 23. Ballots returned by
hand must be submitted to a local board of elections office or an approved ballot drop box by 8 p.m.
A list of locations can be found at vote.md.gov/vote2026.
“Whether voting in person or returning a mail-in ballot, June 23 is the final day to cast your vote in
the primary election,” said State Elections Administrator Jared DeMarinis. “Make a plan to show up,
vote, and shape Maryland’s future. And for mail-in voters, use a drop box to return your ballot today.
Don’t let the USPS changes in the application of a postmark disenfranchise you”
Marylanders who are not currently registered to vote may do so when casting a ballot tomorrow.
They must bring a document that proves where they live when they attempt to vote at their local
polling place.
Primary Election Day is the final opportunity to vote in this year’s primary election. Learn more at
vote.md.gov/vote2026 or download the free Go Vote Maryland! app from the Google Play store or
the Apple store.

title: SBE Primary Early Voting Starts June 2026 ES
text:
Mañana Comienza la Votación Anticipada en Persona para las Elecciones Primarias en Maryland

ANNAPOLIS (10 de junio de 2026) — La Junta Electoral del Estado de Maryland (SBE) les recuerda a los electores que la votación anticipada en persona en las Elecciones Primarias Gubernamentales comienza mañana, jueves 11 de junio.

"La votación anticipada es una opción segura y conveniente para votar en la elección primaria", dijo Jared DeMarinis, Administrador Estatal de Elecciones. "Suele haber una gran participación en la votación anticipada, por lo que les pido a todos los electores de Maryland que estén considerando esta opción que planifiquen con anticipación".

La votación anticipada será todos los días desde el jueves 11 de junio hasta el jueves 18 de junio de 7 a.m. a 8 p.m. Los electores que estén en la fila a las 8 p.m. podrán emitir su voto. La lista completa de centros de votación anticipada está disponible en línea en vote.md.gov/vote2026.

Todavía hay tiempo para registrarse para votar en la elección primaria. Los habitantes de Maryland pueden registrarse cuando vayan a votar durante la votación anticipada o en el Día de la Elección Primaria (martes 23 de junio). Si va a registrarse el día que vota, recuerde llevar un documento que compruebe dónde vive cuando vaya a votar en su centro de votación local o centro de votación anticipada.

La votación anticipada es una de las tres opciones para votar en esta elección. Los otros dos son el voto por correo y el voto en persona el Día de la Elección Primaria, el martes 23 de junio. Para ver más información sobre estas opciones y sobre las elecciones primarias, visite vote.md.gov/vote2026 o descargue la aplicación gratuita Go Vote Maryland! desde Google Play o Apple Store.

title: SBE Deadline Mail In Ballot ES
text: Se acerca la fecha límite para solicitar papeletas de voto por correo ANNAPOLIS (4 de junio de 2026) — La Junta Electoral del Estado de Maryland les recuerda a los electores que se acerca la fecha límite para solicitar una papeleta de voto por correo para las Elecciones Primarias Gubernamentales de 2026. Para que podamos enviarle por fax o por correo postal una papeleta de voto por correo, tenemos que recibir su pedido por internet o por correo postal hasta el 16 de junio de 2026 (sin importar la fecha de envío). Si quiere recibir su papeleta de voto por correo por correo electrónico, envíe la solicitud por internet hasta el viernes 19 de junio de 2026. Visite la página web de voto por correo para solicitar una papeleta. Las papeletas de voto por correo que se devuelvan por correo postal deben tener matasellos con fecha y hora anterior a las 8 p.m. del día de las elecciones primarias, martes 23 de junio. Si se devuelven en mano, las papeletas deben llevarse a un centro de votación anticipada durante la votación anticipada, o dejarse en un buzón electoral o en junta electoral local antes de las 8 p.m. del 23 de junio. Puede encontrar la lista completa de lugares de votación anticipada en vote.md.gov/vote2026. “Ya estamos más cerca de la Elección Primaria, y les pido a todos los electores registrados que tengan listo su plan para votar”, dijo el Administrador Estatal de Elecciones, Jared DeMarinis. "Las papeletas de voto por correo son una opción segura, legal y transparente para emitir su voto. Es importante que pida su papeleta antes de la fecha límite". Los electores registrados tienen otras dos opciones para votar: el voto anticipado en persona o el voto en el Día de la Elección Primaria. 1.

title: SBE Deadline Mail In Ballot ES
text: Es importante que pida su papeleta antes de la fecha límite". Los electores registrados tienen otras dos opciones para votar: el voto anticipado en persona o el voto en el Día de la Elección Primaria. 1. Voto anticipado en persona: Vote en la votación anticipada y olvídese de las filas y las demoras en el Día de la Elección. Fechas: Del jueves 11 al jueves 18 de junio Horario: De 7 a.m. a 8 p.m. todos los días. Si está en la fila antes de las 8 p.m., se le permitirá votar. Tiene a su disposición una lista completa de centros de votación anticipada en vote.md.gov/vote2026 2. Voto el día de la elección en persona: Vote en persona en su centro de votación local el Día de la Elección Primaria, el martes 23 de junio. Horario: Las urnas estarán abiertas de 7 a.m. a 8 p.m. Los electores tienen que votar en su centro de votación asignado. Encuentre su lugar de votación en el sitio web de la SBE. Les recordamos a los electores que hayan solicitado una papeleta de voto por correo antes del 14 de mayo que deben votar la papeleta de reemplazo enviada a fines de mayo. Vote en la papeleta de reemplazo y envíela para asegurarse de que se cuente la papeleta del partido correcto. Para hacer un seguimiento del estado de su papeleta, visite vote.md.gov/search. Puede encontrar más información sobre la Elección Primaria de Maryland, como las fechas límite para entregar la papeleta cuando la complete, en vote.md.gov/vote2026 o descargando la aplicación gratuita Go Vote Maryland! de la tienda Google Play o la tienda Apple. ### Contacto: Bruce Miller, bmiller@kopublicaffairs.com, 410-916-6951 Lexy Rhoden, morgan.rhoden@maryland.gov, 443-924-1644
